thread.title: An Early Apple Bear Is Taking a Victory Lap --- and Upgrading the Stock

author: Barron's
title: An Early Apple Bear Is Taking a Victory Lap --- and Upgrading the Stock

organizations.name: stephanie keith/getty images new street research

text:
Photograph by Stephanie Keith/Getty Images New Street Research analyst Pierre Ferragu, who presciently downgraded Apple stock to Sell in August, is taking his victory lap.
The analyst raised his rating for Apple stock ( AAPL ) to Neutral on Thursday, saying his negative call is now "fully played out" after Apple on Wednesday lowered its revenue forecast for the all-important holiday quarter. Apple stock was down about 9%, to $143 per share, on Thursday following the news.
On Wednesday, Apple said it now expects sales of approximately $84 billion for the December quarter, versus the Wall Street consensus of $91.3 billion, according to FactSet. On Nov. 1, Apple gave a sales outlook range of $89 billion to $93 billion for the December quarter.
Last year, Ferragu predicted Apple's current iPhone product cycle was similar to what happened with the iPhone 6S and 6S Plus in 2015 and 2016, when the popularity of prior models had pulled demand forward.
"This reflects our iPhone X pull-forward thesis playing out in full and deteriorating macro in China," Ferragu wrote in a note Thursday. "We don't see reasons for Apple to underperform further this year."
Ferragu lowered his Apple stock price target to $140, from $165.

"The disappointing performance of the iPhone XR shows... high-end buyers are happy to spend more for a fancier phones," he told Barron's in November . "It is much less true for budget buyers."
At the time, he had the lowest price target for Apple stock on Wall Street.
Apple stock had already declined nearly 30% since the end of October through Wednesday, as concerns had mounted about weak demand for the iPhone models released last fall, amid a number of smartphone supplier warnings.
Apple CEO Tim Cook blamed China as the key driver for Apple's lowered sales guidance. China generated 18% of the company's sales in its September quarter.
"While we anticipated some challenges in key emerging markets, we did not foresee the magnitude of the economic deceleration, particularly in Greater China," Cook said in a statement Wednesday.
